description:
Redwood Inference is formalizing Dedicated capacity guarantees by defining a throughput SLO (what is guaranteed, how it is measured, and under what conditions it applies) and mapping those guarantees to standardized hardware “shapes” and pricing tiers. The goal is to make Dedicated purchases predictable for customers (clear commitments and escalation paths) while keeping Redwood’s fleet and unit economics manageable (standard shapes, consistent capacity accounting, and tier-aware routing/overload behavior).

Scope includes: (1) SLO definition for Dedicated throughput (metrics, measurement window, exclusions like customer-side throttling, model/version constraints, warm pool behavior), (2) tier taxonomy (e.g., Standard / Plus / Premium) with explicit entitlements (throughput floor, burst policy, failover posture, support response targets), (3) hardware shape catalog per region (GPU type, count, CPU/RAM, networking, storage, max batch/ctx recommendations), (4) pricing/packaging mapping from tier→shape(s)→list price and discount guardrails, and (5) internal operationalization: dashboards, alerting, runbooks, and support escalation playbooks.

Primary stakeholders: Product Dedicated (Lauren Bishop) owns tier definitions and customer-facing commitments; Infra/Fleet (Irene Choi, Vanessa Ortiz) owns shapes and provisioning mechanics; SRE (Sean Gallagher, Rafael Mendes) owns SLO semantics, alerting, and error budget policy; Observability (Allison Grant, Sergio Costa) owns instrumentation/dashboards; Finance/FP&A (Laura Bennett, Rishi Malhotra) validates margin assumptions and pricing floors; Sales Enablement + GTM align messaging and quoting guidance; Support/CS operationalize escalations and customer communications.

Timeline/phases (typical): 2–3 week discovery + metric definition, 3–4 week tier+shape design and pricing model, 2–4 week implementation (instrumentation, tier-aware routing/limits, dashboards), followed by limited GA rollout to a small set of Dedicated customers and a retro to adjust tier thresholds and exclusions. Key constraints: heterogeneous GPU supply by region, model-dependent tokens/sec variability, and the need to prevent an SLO definition that can be gamed or creates excessive operational burden.
